options.content: **BPA-Demo Agent Health** — one traffic light per deployed agent (green = all its alerts OK, orange = warning, red = critical, grey = no data yet), followed by each agent's basic metrics. Four distinct telemetry sources feed this dashboard: the **Infrastructure Agent** (host + MySQL DB, via the DB Monitor extension), the **PHP Probe** (inside the PHP process), the **Browser Agent** (inside real visitors' browsers -- client-perceived timing), and the **BPA WebServer Plugin** (inside our Apache server -- server-side per-transaction timing). The Browser Agent and BPA WebServer Plugin observe the *same* requests from two different vantage points; comparing them is how the Network + Overhead section below approximates time spent outside the server.

panels.title: Infrastructure Agent (DB Monitor)
panels.description: Source: Infrastructure Agent's DB Monitor extension, querying MariaDB directly (host + MySQL DB details) -- not derived from application traffic. This light rolls up every Infra Agent alert to its worst current severity.

sourceNameSpecifier.pattern: SuperDomain\|Custom Metric Host \(Virtual\)\|Custom Metric Process \(Virtual\)\|Custom Metric Agent \(Virtual\)

panels.title: PHP Probe Agent (Application)
panels.description: Source: PHP Probe agent, instrumented inside the PHP process itself on the application server. Server-side, code-level timing. This light rolls up every PHP Probe alert (plus the Trouble User alert) to its worst current severity.

attributeNameSpecifier.pattern: Alerts\|BPA-Demo:(Trouble User \- High Response Time|PHP Probe \- .*)

sourceNameSpecifier.pattern: SuperDomain\|Custom Metric Host \(Virtual\)\|Custom Metric Process \(Virtual\)\|Custom Metric Agent \(Virtual\)

panels.title: Browser Agent (RUM)
panels.description: Source: Browser Agent (the BA JavaScript snippet), executed inside a real visitor's browser. Client-perceived timing -- includes network transit and browser rendering, not just server processing. Requires an actual browser running the snippet; the traffic-generator's plain HTTP requests never populate this. This light rolls up every Browser RUM alert to its worst current severity.

sourceNameSpecifier.pattern: SuperDomain\|Custom Metric Host \(Virtual\)\|Custom Metric Process \(Virtual\)\|Custom Metric Agent \(Virtual\)

panels.title: Infrastructure Agent -- Host + MySQL DB (DB Monitor extension)
DB Availability
panels.description: Source: Infrastructure Agent's DB Monitor extension, querying MariaDB directly (host + MySQL DB details) -- not derived from application traffic. 1 = MariaDB is reachable and responding; 0 = the DB Monitor extension cannot reach it.

panels.title: Connection Refusal Rate
panels.description: Source: Infrastructure Agent's DB Monitor extension, querying MariaDB directly (host + MySQL DB details) -- not derived from application traffic. Rate of MariaDB connection attempts refused (e.g. connection limit reached). Normally 0.

panels.title: Buffer Pool Cache Hit Rate (%)
panels.description: Source: Infrastructure Agent's DB Monitor extension, querying MariaDB directly (host + MySQL DB details) -- not derived from application traffic. InnoDB buffer pool cache hit rate. A drop below ~95% suggests the buffer pool is undersized for the working set.

panels.title: Slow Query Rate (%)
panels.description: Source: Infrastructure Agent's DB Monitor extension, querying MariaDB directly (host + MySQL DB details) -- not derived from application traffic. Percentage of queries flagged as slow by MariaDB's slow-query log. Normally 0%.

panels.title: PHP Probe Agent -- Inside the PHP Process
App Response Time (ms)
panels.description: Source: PHP Probe agent, instrumented inside the PHP process itself on the application server. Server-side, code-level timing. Average server-side response time across every tracked frontend URL. The `trouble` demo use case (5000 sequential DB reads) shows up as a sustained spike here.

panels.title: App Error Rate (per interval)
panels.description: Source: PHP Probe agent, instrumented inside the PHP process itself on the application server. Server-side, code-level timing. Application-level errors reported by the PHP probe per measurement interval.

panels.title: App Concurrency
panels.description: Source: PHP Probe agent, instrumented inside the PHP process itself on the application server. Server-side, code-level timing. Number of requests the PHP probe sees executing at the same instant. Baseline is near 0 on this low-traffic demo.

panels.title: DB Backend Response Time (ms)
panels.description: Source: PHP Probe agent, instrumented inside the PHP process itself on the application server. Server-side, code-level timing. Average response time of the PHP app's own calls to the MariaDB backend, as timed from inside the PHP process (not the DB server's own view -- compare against the Infrastructure Agent section above for that).

panels.title: Browser Agent -- Real User Monitoring (client-side, as seen by the browser)
Page Load Time (ms)
panels.description: Source: Browser Agent (the BA JavaScript snippet), executed inside a real visitor's browser. Client-perceived timing -- includes network transit and browser rendering, not just server processing. Requires an actual browser running the snippet; the traffic-generator's plain HTTP requests never populate this. Full page load time per tracked URL, as timed by the browser (navigation start to load complete) -- includes network transit and rendering, not just server response.

attributeNameSpecifier.pattern: Business Segment\|BPA Demo\|[^|]+:Average Page Load Time \(ms\)$

panels.title: Page Hits (per interval)
panels.description: Source: Browser Agent (the BA JavaScript snippet), executed inside a real visitor's browser. Client-perceived timing -- includes network transit and browser rendering, not just server processing. Requires an actual browser running the snippet; the traffic-generator's plain HTTP requests never populate this. Real-browser page views per tracked URL per interval -- a direct count of actual RUM-instrumented page loads, distinct from the PHP Probe's server-side request count.

attributeNameSpecifier.pattern: Business Segment\|BPA Demo\|[^|]+:Page Hits Per Interval$

panels.title: Resource Time To First Byte (ms)
panels.description: Source: Browser Agent (the BA JavaScript snippet), executed inside a real visitor's browser. Client-perceived timing -- includes network transit and browser rendering, not just server processing. Requires an actual browser running the snippet; the traffic-generator's plain HTTP requests never populate this. Time-to-first-byte for individual page sub-resources (CSS, images, third-party scripts) as measured by the browser's own Resource Timing API -- the closest real "time to first response" signal the Browser Agent reports; it's per-resource, not per-page.

attributeNameSpecifier.pattern: Business Segment\|BPA Demo\|.*:Average Time To First Byte \(ms\)$

panels.title: BPA WebServer Plugin -- Inside Our Apache Server (server-side, as seen by the application)
Response Time (ms)
panels.description: Source: BPA WebServer Plugin, running inside our own Apache server (mod_caplugin). Server-side, per-business-transaction timing as seen at the web server tier -- distinct from the Browser Agent's client-side view of the same requests. Total time the BPA module measures for the request, per business transaction. Compare against Backend Server Time (next panel) -- the gap is roughly network + plugin overhead time.

panels.title: Backend Server Time (ms)
panels.description: Source: BPA WebServer Plugin, running inside our own Apache server (mod_caplugin). Server-side, per-business-transaction timing as seen at the web server tier -- distinct from the Browser Agent's client-side view of the same requests. The portion of Response Time (previous panel) actually spent in backend/application processing, as measured by the BPA module.

attributeNameSpecifier.pattern: Business Segment\|\[BPA Demo\][^|]*\|[^|]+:Average Backend Server Time \(ms\)$

panels.title: Responses Per Interval
panels.description: Source: BPA WebServer Plugin, running inside our own Apache server (mod_caplugin). Server-side, per-business-transaction timing as seen at the web server tier -- distinct from the Browser Agent's client-side view of the same requests. Count of responses per business transaction per interval, as seen at the web server tier.

panels.title: Errors Per Interval
panels.description: Source: BPA WebServer Plugin, running inside our own Apache server (mod_caplugin). Server-side, per-business-transaction timing as seen at the web server tier -- distinct from the Browser Agent's client-side view of the same requests. Count of error responses per business transaction per interval, as seen at the web server tier.

panels.title: Network + Overhead Time (Browser Agent vs BPA WebServer Plugin)
BPA Plugin: Response Time vs Backend Server Time (gap ~= network + overhead)
panels.description: Both lines are from the BPA WebServer Plugin (server-side), for the same business transactions: total Response Time and the Backend Server Time portion of it. The visual gap between them approximates time spent outside backend processing -- network transit, plugin overhead, and response transmission. This is a real-data comparison, not a computed single series: a true subtracted "network time" metric would need a Grafana calculateField transform whose exact behavior on this dx-do build's AIOps NASS datasource plugin couldn't be visually verified (no dashboard-render available here) -- treat this panel as the verified starting point and add that transform via the console's own panel editor, where the actual field names are visible, if you want a single computed series instead of two lines to eyeball.

attributeNameSpecifier.pattern: Business Segment\|\[BPA Demo\][^|]*\|[^|]+:Average Backend Server Time \(ms\)$

list.name: deployment
list.label: Deployment
list.description: Filters the Infrastructure Agent and PHP Probe panels by which deployment reported the data (their identity is DEPLOYMENT_NAME-DEPLOYMENT_POSTFIX from .config, e.g. bpa-demo-docker / bpa-demo-k8s -- see CLAUDE.md's 'Deployment identity' section). Does NOT affect the Browser Agent / BPA WebServer Plugin panels -- those ride a shared DxC Agent identity with no per-deployment distinction available.
